name: nvdisasm-re
description: SASS decoding, semantics, p-code, decompilation, emulation

paragraphs: Assemble SASS source or upload a CUDA .cubin and explore what nvdisasm-re recovers from NVIDIA's nvdisasm:

Emulation needs each architecture's launch-constant layout (known for all but SM107). nvcc's SM90+ code reaches global memory through explicit descriptors, whose semantics are still opaque, so whole kernels run on SM75-SM89.

Every architecture nvdisasm 13.4 describes is supported: SM75, SM80, SM86, SM89, SM90, SM100, SM101, SM103, SM107 and SM120 (SM87/SM88, SM110 and SM121 cubins decode as SM86, SM101 and SM120, as in nvdisasm).
features: Disassembly: the pure-Python decoder (pydecode), which matches nvdisasm's text, with the machine-description class each word matched.
Lifted IR: Ghidra-free instruction semantics as register writes, stores and control flow.
P-code: Ghidra's p-code per instruction from the generated SLEIGH languages (SM75–SM120, exact or readable floating point).
High p-code and Decompiled C: Ghidra's decompiler on the whole kernel, as its simplified SSA p-code per basic block and as C.
Emulate: run a kernel in Ghidra's p-code emulator and, per thread, in the Python evaluator, and compare the traces step by step.
